title: Past action and the requirement of exchange
shortTitle: Past action and the requirement of exchange
summary: Conduct already completed cannot ordinarily be the requested price of a later promise.
notes: Feinberg’s past service explains the employer’s generosity but was not induced by the later pension. Her additional eighteen months of service were likewise not demanded by the resolution as its price. The problem concerning a benefactor’s past gift and a later naming assurance asks about timing and separate promises. The first page of Mills introduces moral obligation, but the remainder of that opinion is outside the assigned ranges.

sources.label: Farnsworth et al., Contracts: Cases and Materials, 10th ed. (2023), pp. 69–74. Open assigned page 69.
